# 成语 (chengyu): four-character idioms.
# One block per topic ("@Topic"), one idiom per line, fields separated by " | ":
#   成语 | literal meaning | what it means | background (story or usage) | example (Chinese) | example (English) | tier
# tier: 1 = everyday, 2 = common, 3 = literary.  Pinyin is generated by tools/annotate.py (add 词[pin1 yin1] hints in the example if needed).

@Animals
画蛇添足 | draw a snake and add feet | To ruin something by adding what it does not need. | In a story from the Warring States Strategies, men raced to draw a snake. The first to finish added feet, so his snake no longer counted as a snake, and he lost the prize of wine. | 这篇文章已经很清楚了，再加一段就是画蛇添足。 | The article is already clear. Adding another paragraph would only spoil it. | 2
守株待兔 | wait by a stump for a hare | To wait for luck instead of making an effort. | The philosopher Han Feizi told of a farmer who saw a hare run into a tree stump and die. He gave up farming to wait by the stump for more hares. | 想成功不能守株待兔，要自己去努力。 | If you want to succeed, you cannot sit and wait for luck. You have to work. | 2
亡羊补牢 | mend the pen after a sheep is lost | It is not too late to fix a problem, even after a loss. | A minister told the king of Chu that a man who mends his pen after losing a sheep can still save the rest of his flock. | 这次考试没考好，现在亡羊补牢，还来得及。 | You did badly on this exam, but if you fix your study now, it is not too late. | 2
对牛弹琴 | play the lute to an ox | To speak to someone who cannot understand. | The oxen in the old tale hear the music but cannot appreciate it. The idiom is often used with humour, or with a little scorn. | 他一点儿也不懂音乐，你跟他谈这个，真是对牛弹琴。 | He knows nothing about music, so talking to him about it is like playing the lute to an ox. | 2
井底之蛙 | the frog at the bottom of a well | A person with a narrow view of the world. | In the Zhuangzi, a frog in a well thinks the sky is only as big as the round opening above it, until a turtle from the sea tells it about the ocean. | 多出去看看吧，别做井底之蛙。 | Go out and see more, and do not be a frog in a well. | 2
狐假虎威 | the fox borrows the tiger's might | To bully others by using a powerful person's name. | In the Strategies of the Warring States, a fox that was caught by a tiger told it to walk behind and watch the animals run. They ran from the tiger, not from the fox. | 他只是经理的朋友，却狐假虎威，对同事发脾气。 | He is only the manager's friend, but he throws his weight around at his colleagues. | 2
杯弓蛇影 | the bow in the cup looks like a snake | To be afraid of something that is not there. | A man drank wine and saw a snake in his cup. He fell ill from fear, until he learned it was only the reflection of a bow hanging on the wall. | 她一听到声音就害怕，真是杯弓蛇影。 | She is scared by every little sound, as if she saw a snake in every cup. | 3
虎头蛇尾 | a tiger's head and a snake's tail | A strong start and a weak finish. | Used for plans, projects and books that begin with a lot of energy and then fade away. | 他做事总是虎头蛇尾，开始很认真，后来就不管了。 | He always starts a task with energy and then loses interest. | 2
鹤立鸡群 | a crane standing among chickens | To stand out clearly from the crowd. | Used as a compliment, often about someone's height or talent. | 他又高又帅，站在人群里鹤立鸡群。 | He is tall and handsome and stands out in the crowd. | 2
一箭双雕 | one arrow, two eagles | To achieve two goals with one action. | A general of the Northern dynasties was said to have shot two eagles with a single arrow. It is the Chinese cousin of "killing two birds with one stone". | 骑车上班既锻炼身体又省钱，真是一箭双雕。 | Cycling to work is exercise and saves money, which kills two birds with one stone. | 2
马到成功 | success arrives as soon as the horse does | Quick success. | A traditional good-luck wish, popular at the start of a new business or a journey. | 祝你新工作马到成功！ | I wish you quick success in your new job! | 1
鸦雀无声 | not even a crow or sparrow makes a sound | Complete silence. | Used for rooms and crowds that suddenly go quiet. | 老师一走进来，教室里就鸦雀无声了。 | As soon as the teacher walked in, the classroom went silent. | 2
九牛一毛 | one hair from nine oxen | A tiny part of something large. | The historian Sima Qian used it to say that his own death would count for no more than a hair on nine oxen. | 这点钱对他来说只是九牛一毛。 | This little money is a drop in the ocean for him. | 3
如鱼得水 | like a fish that has found water | To be in one's element. | In the Three Kingdoms period, Liu Bei said he was like a fish that had found water after he met the strategist Zhuge Liang. | 到了新公司，他如鱼得水，做得很开心。 | At the new company he is in his element and enjoys the work. | 2
老马识途 | an old horse knows the way | An experienced person can show the way. | Han Feizi tells how an army lost its way and followed old horses, which led it home. | 这条路他走了二十年，真是老马识途。 | He has walked this road for twenty years, so he knows it like an old horse. | 3
守口如瓶 | keep your mouth shut like a bottle | To keep a secret. | A bottle with its cap on lets nothing out. It is often used for official secrets and private matters. | 这件事请你一定要守口如瓶。 | Please keep this matter strictly to yourself. | 2

@Numbers
一举两得 | one move, two gains | To gain two things with one action. | A common way to praise a clever plan. | 在国外工作，既能赚钱又能学语言，真是一举两得。 | Working abroad earns money and teaches a language, so you gain two things at once. | 1
三心二意 | three hearts and two minds | To be undecided or half-hearted. | Used to criticise someone who cannot give one thing their full attention. | 学习的时候不要三心二意。 | Do not be half-hearted when you study. | 1
七上八下 | seven up, eight down | To feel nervous and uneasy. | The numbers describe a heart that jumps up and down like buckets in a well. | 等考试成绩的时候，我心里七上八下。 | While I waited for my exam results, I felt very nervous. | 2
九死一生 | nine deaths and one life | To escape from great danger. | Often used for accidents, wars and serious illness. | 他在地震中九死一生，现在已经没事了。 | He barely survived the earthquake, and now he is fine. | 2
十全十美 | ten parts complete, ten parts beautiful | Perfect in every way. | Often used in the negative: nothing in this world is perfect. | 世界上没有十全十美的人。 | Nobody in this world is perfect. | 1
五花八门 | five flowers and eight doors | Of every kind; a great variety. | The phrase first described changing military formations. Now it means a wide range of things. | 超市里的饮料五花八门，我不知道买哪一种。 | The drinks in the supermarket are so varied that I do not know which to buy. | 2
一心一意 | one heart, one mind | Wholeheartedly; with full attention. | Used for work, study and love alike. | 他一心一意地照顾生病的妈妈。 | He looks after his sick mother with all his heart. | 1
千方百计 | a thousand methods and a hundred plans | To try every possible means. | Often used for hard goals that require a lot of effort. | 他千方百计想考上大学。 | He tried every way he could to get into university. | 2
百发百中 | a hundred shots, a hundred hits | To hit the target every time. | The archer Yang Youji of the Spring and Autumn period was famous for hitting a willow leaf from a hundred paces. Now it is used for shooting, sports and predictions. | 他打篮球投篮百发百中。 | He never misses a shot at basketball. | 2
一见钟情 | love at first sight | To fall in love at first sight. | 钟情 means to give one's love. | 他们在朋友的婚礼上一见钟情。 | They fell in love at first sight at a friend's wedding. | 1
万无一失 | ten thousand times without one mistake | Completely safe and sure. | Used for plans and arrangements. | 这个办法万无一失，你放心吧。 | This method is completely safe, so do not worry. | 2
三番五次 | three times, five times | Again and again. | Used for repeated actions, often annoying ones. | 我三番五次地提醒他，他还是忘了。 | I reminded him again and again, but he still forgot. | 2
一帆风顺 | a smooth sail | Smooth progress with no trouble. | A very common good-luck wish for studies, work and travel. | 祝你一帆风顺！ | I wish you smooth sailing! | 1
四面八方 | four sides and eight directions | From all directions. | Used for crowds and voices that come from every side. | 参加比赛的人来自四面八方。 | The people at the contest came from all over. | 1

@Study and effort
愚公移山 | the Foolish Old Man moves the mountains | With perseverance, even the hardest task can be done. | In an old tale, an old man decided to dig away two mountains in front of his house. When laughed at, he said his sons and grandsons would carry on. Heaven moved the mountains for him. | 只要有愚公移山的精神，就没有做不成的事。 | With the spirit of the Foolish Old Man, nothing is impossible. | 2
铁杵成针 | an iron rod becomes a needle | Patience can achieve anything. | Legend says the young poet Li Bai met an old woman who was grinding an iron rod into a needle. He understood that persistence pays off and went back to his books. | 学汉字要像铁杵成针一样，慢慢来。 | Learning characters takes patience, like grinding an iron rod into a needle. | 2
滴水穿石 | dripping water pierces stone | Small efforts, kept up, can achieve great things. | A drop of water is weak, but drop after drop wears through a rock. | 每天读十分钟，滴水穿石，一年后你会有很大进步。 | Read for ten minutes a day, and after a year you will have improved a great deal. | 2
持之以恒 | hold on to it with constancy | To keep at something steadily. | Often said about exercise, study and good habits. | 学外语最重要的是持之以恒。 | The most important thing in learning a language is to keep at it. | 2
废寝忘食 | give up sleep and forget meals | To be so absorbed that one forgets to eat or sleep. | Used as praise for hard workers, or with a smile for people who are hooked on a game. | 他为了准备考试，废寝忘食地复习。 | He studied day and night, forgetting to eat and sleep, to prepare for the exam. | 2
凿壁偷光 | bore through the wall to borrow light | To study hard in spite of poverty. | The Han-dynasty scholar Kuang Heng was too poor to buy candles. He made a hole in the wall to read by the light of his neighbour's house. | 古时候有凿壁偷光的故事，说明学习不怕穷。 | The old story of boring through the wall shows that poverty need not stop anyone from studying. | 3
悬梁刺股 | tie hair to a beam, prick the thigh | To study with great determination. | Two scholars, Sun Jing and Su Qin, were said to keep themselves awake at night like this. It describes hard study. | 为了考上大学，他每天悬梁刺股地学习。 | To get into university, he studies as hard as the scholars of old. | 3
熟能生巧 | skill comes from familiarity | Practice makes perfect. | Used to encourage people who feel stuck while learning a skill. | 别着急，熟能生巧，多练习就好了。 | Do not worry. Practice makes perfect, so keep trying. | 1
举一反三 | learn one, infer three | To learn many things from one example. | Confucius said he would only teach a student who could work out the other three corners after being shown one. | 好学生会举一反三，不是只会背答案。 | A good student can infer other cases and does not just memorise answers. | 2
温故知新 | review the old to learn the new | To gain new insight by reviewing the past. | This line comes from the Analects of Confucius. | 复习以前的课文，也是一种温故知新。 | Reviewing old lessons is also a way to find something new. | 2
精益求精 | good, and still better | To always try to do better. | Used for crafts, products and skills. | 这家饭馆的师傅对每道菜都精益求精。 | The chef at this restaurant always tries to improve every dish. | 2
半途而废 | give up halfway | To quit before finishing. | The idiom often appears in the advice that one should never give up halfway. | 做事不能半途而废。 | You must not give up halfway. | 2
马马虎虎[ma3 ma3 hu3 hu3] | horse, horse, tiger, tiger | So-so; careless. | It has two meanings. As an answer to "How are you?" or "How was it?", it means "so-so". About a task, it means careless. | 他做作业总是马马虎虎，所以错误很多。 | He does his homework carelessly, so he makes many mistakes. | 1
一丝不苟 | not one thread is careless | Very careful and exact. | Praise for people who do detailed work with great care. | 这位老师对工作一丝不苟。 | This teacher is meticulous in her work. | 2
事半功倍 | half the work, double the result | To get twice the result with half the effort. | Said of good methods and tools. | 找对方法，学习会事半功倍。 | When you find the right method, you learn with much less effort. | 2
勤能补拙 | diligence makes up for clumsiness | Hard work can make up for lack of talent. | A common saying to encourage people who think they are not clever enough. | 我不聪明，但是勤能补拙。 | I am not clever, but hard work makes up for it. | 2
学无止境 | there is no end to learning | There is always more to learn. | Often said by teachers, and often written on school walls. | 学无止境，活到老，学到老。 | There is no end to learning. You learn as long as you live. | 1

@Character
自食其力 | eat from one's own strength | To support oneself by one's own work. | Used for people who earn their own living. | 他十八岁就开始自食其力。 | He started to earn his own living at eighteen. | 2
助人为乐 | find joy in helping others | To take pleasure in helping others. | A traditional virtue that schools teach children. | 他助人为乐，邻居都喜欢他。 | He enjoys helping others, and all his neighbours like him. | 1
见义勇为 | see what is right and act bravely | To step in bravely for a just cause. | Often used in news about people who stop a thief or save someone in danger. | 这位年轻人见义勇为，救了一个孩子。 | This young man bravely stepped in and saved a child. | 2
谦虚谨慎 | modest and careful | Modest and prudent. | A quality that schools and employers like to praise. | 取得了好成绩，也要谦虚谨慎。 | Even when you do well, you should stay modest. | 2
口是心非 | the mouth says yes, the heart says no | To say one thing and mean another. | Used for people who are not sincere. | 他嘴上说喜欢，其实是口是心非。 | He says he likes it, but he does not mean it. | 2
言行一致 | words and deeds agree | To do what one says. | A virtue for leaders and teachers. | 老师要求我们，自己也要言行一致。 | The teacher asks things of us and must also do them himself. | 2
言而有信 | one's word can be trusted | To keep one's word. | In the Analects, Confucius says that a person who cannot be trusted is like a cart without the pin that joins it to its shafts. | 做人要言而有信。 | A person should keep their word. | 1
一言为定 | one word settles it | It is a deal. | Said at the end of an agreement. | 我们明天八点见，一言为定！ | We meet at eight tomorrow, and that is settled! | 1
说到做到 | when said, it is done | To do what one says. | Used for promises. | 他说到做到，从来不骗人。 | He does what he says and never lies. | 1
脚踏实地 | feet on solid ground | Down-to-earth; practical and steady. | Praise for people who work hard and do not dream of quick results. | 想成功就要脚踏实地。 | If you want to succeed, you have to be down-to-earth. | 1
自高自大 | think oneself high and great | Arrogant. | Used to warn against pride. | 他取得了一点成绩就自高自大。 | He became arrogant after a little success. | 2
心直口快 | an honest heart and a quick mouth | Straightforward and outspoken. | Someone who says what they think at once. | 她心直口快，有什么话就说什么。 | She is outspoken and says whatever is on her mind. | 2
胸有成竹 | having a complete bamboo in one's chest | To have a clear plan in mind. | The painter Wen Tong painted bamboo only after he could see the whole plant in his mind. | 面试的时候他胸有成竹，一点儿也不紧张。 | He had a clear plan for the interview and was not at all nervous. | 2

@Stories from history
刻舟求剑 | notch the boat to find the sword | To act stubbornly without noticing that things have changed. | In a story from the Lüshi Chunqiu, a man dropped his sword from a boat and carved a mark on the side. He then waited for the boat to land to look for the sword under the mark. | 现在时代变了，还用老办法就是刻舟求剑。 | Times have changed, and using the old methods is like marking the boat to find the sword. | 2
掩耳盗铃 | cover one's ears to steal a bell | To fool oneself. | A thief wanted to steal a bell, but it rang when he touched it. He covered his own ears and thought nobody else would hear it either. | 不告诉别人，错误也还在，那是掩耳盗铃。 | If you do not tell anyone, the mistake is still there. You are only fooling yourself. | 2
自相矛盾 | one's spear and shield contradict | To contradict oneself. | Han Feizi told of a man who sold a spear that could pierce anything, and a shield that nothing could pierce. A customer asked what would happen if the spear struck the shield. | 他前后说的话自相矛盾。 | What he said before and after contradict each other. | 2
买椟还珠 | buy the box and return the pearl | To choose the wrong thing and miss the real value. | A man bought a pearl in a beautiful box and kept the box. He gave the pearl back. | 买礼物只看包装，是买椟还珠。 | Choosing a gift for its wrapping alone is like keeping the box and returning the pearl. | 3
揠苗助长 | pull the seedlings to help them grow | To ruin something by being too impatient. | In the Mencius, a farmer in Song pulled each of his seedlings a little to help them grow. By evening they had all died. | 教育孩子不能揠苗助长。 | You cannot educate a child by pushing too hard. | 2
邯郸学步 | learn to walk like the people of Handan | To lose one's own style while imitating others. | In the Zhuangzi, a young man went to the city of Handan to learn its way of walking. He forgot his own and had to crawl home. | 学别人要有自己的特点，不要邯郸学步。 | When you learn from others, keep your own character and do not lose it. | 3
画龙点睛 | paint the dragon and dot its eyes | To add the key touch that makes it come alive. | The painter Zhang Sengyou was said to have painted four dragons on a wall without eyes. When he added the eyes of two, they flew away. | 文章最后一句真是画龙点睛。 | The last sentence of the essay is the finishing touch. | 2
望梅止渴 | look at plums to quench thirst | To comfort oneself with an empty hope. | Cao Cao told his thirsty army that a grove of plum trees lay ahead. The thought of sour plums made their mouths water. | 光想没有用，不能望梅止渴。 | Only thinking about it is of no use. You cannot quench your thirst by looking at plums. | 2
三顾茅庐 | visit the thatched hut three times | To invite someone with great sincerity. | The warlord Liu Bei visited the hut of Zhuge Liang three times before the strategist agreed to help him. | 公司三顾茅庐，请他来当经理。 | The company went to him again and again until he agreed to be the manager. | 2
破釜沉舟 | smash the cooking pots and sink the boats | To act with total commitment, with no way back. | Xiang Yu led his army across a river and destroyed the boats and the pots, so that the soldiers had no choice but to fight. They won. | 他破釜沉舟，辞了工作去创业。 | He burned his bridges, quit his job and started his own business. | 2
卧薪尝胆 | sleep on brushwood and taste gall | To endure hardship and prepare for revenge or a big goal. | After he lost a war, King Goujian of Yue slept on brushwood and tasted bitter gall every day so that he would not forget his shame. He later won his country back. | 他卧薪尝胆，终于在比赛中获胜。 | He endured years of hard work and finally won the contest. | 3
纸上谈兵 | talk about war on paper | To talk about theory with no practical ability. | The young general Zhao Kuo knew all the military books but lost a major battle when he commanded a real army. | 只看书不实践，就是纸上谈兵。 | Reading books without practising is only talk on paper. | 2
四面楚歌 | Chu songs on all four sides | To be surrounded by enemies and have no help. | When Xiang Yu's army was surrounded, the enemy sang songs of Chu. He thought they had already taken his homeland. | 公司遇到困难，他感到四面楚歌。 | When the company ran into trouble, he felt he had enemies on every side. | 2
一鸣惊人 | one call that astonishes everyone | To suddenly achieve something remarkable after a quiet start. | King Zhuang of Chu ignored state affairs for three years. A minister asked him about a bird that neither flew nor sang. The king replied that when it flew, it would reach the sky, and when it sang, it would astonish everyone. | 他一鸣惊人，第一本书就卖了一百万本。 | His first book sold a million copies, and the whole world was astonished. | 2
完璧归赵 | return the jade to Zhao intact | To return something to its owner in perfect condition. | The envoy Lin Xiangru brought a precious jade to the powerful state of Qin and brought it safely home when the king of Qin broke his promise. | 书我看完了，现在完璧归赵。 | I have finished the book, and now I return it to you in perfect condition. | 3
背水一战 | fight with the river at one's back | To fight with no way of retreat. | The general Han Xin put his army with its back to a river so that the soldiers had to fight to survive. | 这次考试是背水一战，必须通过。 | This exam is a do-or-die moment, and I must pass. | 3

@Friends and family
志同道合 | the same goals, the same path | To share the same ideals. | Used for friends and partners who see the world alike. | 我们几个志同道合的朋友一起开了一家书店。 | A few like-minded friends and I opened a bookshop together. | 2
一见如故 | like old friends at the first meeting | To feel close from the first meeting. | Used when two people feel they have known each other for a long time. | 我和她一见如故，聊了一晚上。 | She and I felt like old friends and talked all night. | 2
情同手足 | feelings like hands and feet | As close as brothers or sisters. | Hands and feet are parts of one body. | 他们俩情同手足。 | The two of them are as close as brothers. | 2
相依为命 | depend on each other for life | To depend on each other to survive. | Often used for family members who have only each other. | 奶奶和孙子相依为命。 | The grandmother and her grandson depend on each other. | 2
同甘共苦 | share sweet and bitter | To share both good and hard times. | Used for couples, friends and teams. | 我们一起同甘共苦了十年。 | We have shared the good and the bad for ten years. | 2
青梅竹马 | green plums and a bamboo horse | Childhood friends who grew up together. | A line in a poem by Li Bai describes a boy riding a bamboo horse and a girl picking green plums. | 他们是青梅竹马，从小就认识。 | They are childhood friends who have known each other since they were small. | 2
天伦之乐 | the joy of natural family ties | The happiness of a family. | Often said of grandparents who live with their children and grandchildren. | 退休以后，他在家享受天伦之乐。 | After he retired, he enjoyed the happiness of family life at home. | 2
白头偕老 | grow old together till the hair is white | To stay together as a couple to old age. | A traditional wish for newly-weds. | 祝你们白头偕老！ | I wish you a long and happy life together! | 2
高山流水 | high mountains and flowing water | A deep friendship in which people truly understand each other. | The musician Bo Ya played tunes about mountains and rivers. Only his friend Zhong Ziqi understood them. When Zhong Ziqi died, Bo Ya broke his zither. | 他们是高山流水般的知音。 | They are soulmates who truly understand each other. | 3
孟母三迁 | Mencius's mother moved three times | A parent who works hard to give a child a good environment. | The mother of the philosopher Mencius moved house three times, from near a graveyard and a market to near a school. | 为了孩子上学，他们像孟母三迁一样搬了家。 | They moved house for their child's school, just like Mencius's mother. | 2
尊老爱幼 | respect the old and love the young | To respect the elderly and care for children. | A basic virtue on buses and in families. | 在中国，尊老爱幼是一种传统。 | In China, respecting the old and caring for the young is a tradition. | 1
举案齐眉 | raise the tray to eyebrow height | Mutual respect between husband and wife. | Liang Hong's wife Meng Guang lifted the food tray to the height of her eyebrows when she served him, as a sign of respect. | 他们夫妻举案齐眉，让人羡慕。 | The couple respect each other, and others envy them. | 3

@Wisdom and warnings
塞翁失马 | the old man at the border loses his horse | A loss may turn out to be a blessing. | In the Huainanzi, an old man's horse ran away. He said it might be lucky. The horse came back with another horse, then his son fell off it and broke a leg, which later saved him from the army. | 他丢了工作，后来找到了更好的，真是塞翁失马。 | He lost his job and later found a better one. It was a blessing in disguise. | 2
未雨绸缪 | mend the window before it rains | To prepare before trouble comes. | The line comes from the Book of Songs, where a bird repairs its nest before the rain. | 我们要未雨绸缪，先存一点钱。 | We should prepare in advance and save some money first. | 3
居安思危 | in peace, think of danger | To be alert to danger in good times. | A line from the Zuo Zhuan. | 公司赚钱的时候也要居安思危。 | Even when the company is making money, it must be alert to danger. | 2
实事求是 | seek truth from facts | To be practical and base decisions on facts. | A phrase from the Book of Han that became a famous slogan in modern China. | 做研究一定要实事求是。 | In research one must always stick to the facts. | 2
三思而行 | think three times and act | To think carefully before acting. | The Analects say that Ji Wenzi thought three times before acting. Confucius said that twice was enough. | 买房子是大事，要三思而行。 | Buying a flat is a big matter, so think carefully before you act. | 2
前车之鉴 | the overturned cart ahead is a warning | A past failure that serves as a lesson. | The cart that overturned in front of you warns you of the danger on the road. | 他的失败是我们的前车之鉴。 | His failure is a lesson for us. | 3
因小失大 | lose the big by caring about the small | To lose something big while trying to save something small. | Used for people who want to save a little money and end up losing a lot. | 为了省几块钱买便宜货，结果坏了，真是因小失大。 | He bought a cheap item to save a few yuan, and it broke, so he lost more in the end. | 2
得不偿失 | what is gained does not make up for the loss | The cost is greater than the benefit. | Used for decisions that do not pay off. | 熬夜工作，把身体搞坏了，得不偿失。 | Working late until you ruin your health is not worth it. | 2
开卷有益 | opening a book is beneficial | Reading always does you good. | A saying linked to Emperor Taizong of Song, who set himself to read three volumes of a huge encyclopedia every day. | 开卷有益，每天读一点书吧。 | Reading always does you good, so read a little every day. | 2
入乡随俗 | when entering a village, follow its customs | When in Rome, do as the Romans do. | Used for travellers and newcomers. | 到了中国，要入乡随俗，用筷子吃饭。 | In China, do as the locals do and eat with chopsticks. | 1
世外桃源 | a peach-blossom land beyond the world | An ideal place, quiet and far from the world. | The poet Tao Yuanming wrote about a fisherman who found a hidden village where people had lived in peace for hundreds of years. | 这个山村像世外桃源一样安静。 | This mountain village is as quiet as a paradise. | 2
取长补短 | take the long to make up for the short | To learn from each other's strengths. | Used for teams, schools and companies. | 我们互相学习，取长补短。 | We learn from each other and make up for our weak points. | 2
集思广益 | gather ideas and widen the benefit | To pool ideas for a better result. | Used in meetings and discussions. | 大家集思广益，一定能想出好办法。 | If we all share ideas, we can find a good solution. | 3
青出于蓝 | blue comes from the indigo plant | The student surpasses the teacher. | The Xunzi says that blue dye comes from the indigo plant but is bluer than the plant itself. | 他的画比老师的还好，真是青出于蓝。 | His paintings are better than his teacher's. The student has surpassed the master. | 3
雪中送炭 | send charcoal in the snow | To help someone when they need it most. | A help that comes at the right moment. It is the opposite of 锦上添花. | 在我最困难的时候，你雪中送炭，我永远忘不了。 | You helped me at my hardest time, and I will never forget it. | 2
锦上添花 | add flowers to brocade | To add something good to what is already good. | The opposite of 雪中送炭 (charcoal in the snow). | 他过生日那天，朋友们都送来了鲜花，真是锦上添花。 | On his birthday all his friends sent flowers, which was the icing on the cake. | 2
画饼充饥 | draw a cake to ease hunger | To comfort oneself with empty fantasies. | In the Three Kingdoms period, an official wrote that a painted cake cannot satisfy hunger. | 光想不做，只是画饼充饥。 | Just thinking without acting is like drawing a cake to quench hunger. | 3
杀鸡取卵 | kill the hen to get the egg | To sacrifice long-term gain for a short-term profit. | It is like cutting open a hen to take all her eggs at once, and so losing the hen. | 过度捕鱼是杀鸡取卵。 | Overfishing is killing the hen to get the eggs. | 2
爱屋及乌 | love the house and the crows on it | To love everything connected to someone you love. | Used for people whose affection extends to the loved one's relatives and belongings. | 他爱屋及乌，连女朋友的小狗也很喜欢。 | His love for her extends to everything around her, even her little dog. | 3
多此一举 | an unnecessary move | To do something unnecessary. | Used for actions that add nothing. | 你已经带伞了，再带雨衣就是多此一举。 | You already have an umbrella, so taking a raincoat too is unnecessary. | 2
好事多磨 | good things take much grinding | Good things come only after setbacks. | A saying used for weddings and big plans that go slowly. | 好事多磨，别着急。 | Good things take time, so do not worry. | 2
破镜重圆 | a broken mirror made whole again | A couple reunited after being apart. | A husband and wife broke a mirror in two when war forced them apart, and each kept a half. Years later the halves were matched and the couple were together again. | 他们分手后又和好了，真是破镜重圆。 | They got back together after breaking up, like a broken mirror made whole. | 3

@Nature
春暖花开 | spring is warm and flowers open | Spring at its best. | Often used in letters and greetings in spring. | 春暖花开的时候，我们去公园玩吧。 | When spring comes and the flowers open, let us go to the park. | 1
鸟语花香 | birds sing and flowers smell sweet | A lovely spring scene. | Used for gardens and the countryside. | 春天的公园里鸟语花香。 | In spring the park is full of birdsong and the scent of flowers. | 1
风和日丽 | gentle wind and bright sun | Mild and sunny weather. | Used for perfect days out. | 今天风和日丽，适合出去玩。 | The weather is mild and sunny today, so it is good for going out. | 2
山清水秀 | green hills and clear water | Beautiful scenery. | Used for lovely landscapes, such as Guilin. | 桂林的风景山清水秀。 | The scenery of Guilin has green hills and clear water. | 2
万紫千红 | ten thousand purples and a thousand reds | A rich variety of colours. | Used for gardens in full bloom. | 花园里万紫千红，漂亮极了。 | The garden is full of colour and looks beautiful. | 2
秋高气爽 | high autumn sky and fresh air | Clear, cool autumn weather. | Used to describe the best season in northern China. | 北京的秋天秋高气爽。 | Autumn in Beijing is clear and fresh. | 2
冰天雪地 | an ice sky and a snow ground | A world of ice and snow. | Used for cold, snowy places like Harbin. | 东北的冬天冰天雪地。 | Winter in the northeast is a world of ice and snow. | 1
一望无际 | as far as the eye can see, no end | Stretching endlessly. | Used for the sea, plains and deserts. | 站在山上，可以看到一望无际的大海。 | On top of the mountain, you can see the endless sea. | 2
日新月异 | new by the day, different by the month | To change rapidly. | Often used of cities, technology and the economy. | 中国的城市发展日新月异。 | Chinese cities change rapidly. | 2
天长地久 | as long as heaven and earth | Everlasting. | Used for love, friendship and wishes. | 愿我们的友谊天长地久。 | May our friendship last forever. | 2
沧海桑田 | the blue sea turns into mulberry fields | Great changes over a long time. | A legend tells of an immortal who saw the sea turn into mulberry fields three times. | 这个地方几十年没来，真是沧海桑田。 | I have not been here for decades, and everything has changed. | 3

@Feelings and daily life
目不转睛 | the eyes do not turn | To stare without looking away. | Used for children watching TV or people watching a show. | 孩子目不转睛地看着电视。 | The child watched TV without looking away. | 2
津津有味 | with great relish | With great enjoyment. | Used for eating, reading and listening. | 他津津有味地吃着饺子。 | He ate the dumplings with great pleasure. | 2
狼吞虎咽 | swallow like a wolf and gulp like a tiger | To eat greedily and fast. | Used when someone is very hungry. | 他饿坏了，狼吞虎咽地吃了三碗饭。 | He was starving and wolfed down three bowls of rice. | 2
垂头丧气 | head drooping, spirits low | Dejected. | Used for people who have just lost or failed. | 比赛输了，大家都垂头丧气。 | We lost the match, and everybody looked dejected. | 2
手忙脚乱 | hands busy and feet in a mess | To be flustered and rushed. | Used for sudden busy moments. | 客人突然来了，妈妈手忙脚乱。 | The guests came suddenly, and Mum was in a flurry. | 2
无精打采 | without spirit or colour | Listless. | Used for people who feel tired or sad. | 他昨天没睡好，今天无精打采。 | He did not sleep well last night and is listless today. | 2
兴高采烈 | high spirits and bright colour | In high spirits. | Used for people who are very happy. | 孩子们兴高采烈地去春游。 | The children set off on their spring outing in high spirits. | 2
喜出望外 | joy beyond one's hopes | Overjoyed at an unexpected good thing. | Used for surprises. | 听到好消息，我喜出望外。 | I was overjoyed to hear the good news. | 2
迫不及待 | too urgent to wait | Unable to wait. | Used for people who are eager to do something. | 孩子们迫不及待地打开礼物。 | The children could not wait to open their presents. | 2
左右为难 | difficult on both the left and the right | To be in a dilemma. | Used when both choices are bad. | 两个工作都很好，我左右为难。 | Both jobs are good, and I cannot decide. | 2
哭笑不得 | not knowing whether to cry or laugh | To find it both funny and annoying. | Used for silly situations. | 孩子把我的手机放进了水里，我真是哭笑不得。 | My child put my phone in the water, and I did not know whether to laugh or cry. | 2
目瞪口呆 | eyes wide and mouth open | To be stunned. | Used for big surprises. | 看到那么多人，他目瞪口呆。 | When he saw so many people, he was stunned. | 2
不知所措 | not knowing what to do | To be at a loss. | Used for sudden, confusing situations. | 第一次上台讲话，她不知所措。 | The first time she spoke on stage, she did not know what to do. | 2
讨价还价 | ask a price and bargain back | To bargain. | A usual activity at markets in China. | 在小店买东西可以讨价还价。 | You can bargain when you shop at small stores. | 1
物美价廉 | good goods and a low price | Good quality at a low price. | Common in shop advertisements. | 这家店的东西物美价廉。 | Things in this shop are good and cheap. | 2
人山人海 | people mountain, people sea | A huge crowd. | Used for festivals and holidays. | 国庆节的时候，公园里人山人海。 | On National Day, the park is packed with people. | 1
车水马龙 | carriages like flowing water and horses like dragons | A busy street full of traffic. | Used for busy streets and cities. | 街上车水马龙，很热闹。 | The street is busy with traffic and full of life. | 2
络绎不绝 | an unbroken stream | A constant flow of people. | Used for visitors and customers who keep coming. | 长城上的游客络绎不绝。 | Visitors on the Great Wall keep coming without a break. | 3
无可奈何 | nothing can be done about it | Helpless; with no way out. | Used when a person has no choice. | 事情已经这样了，我也无可奈何。 | It is already like this, and I am helpless. | 2
全心全意 | with all one's heart and mind | Wholeheartedly. | Used for work and service. | 医生全心全意地为病人服务。 | The doctor serves patients wholeheartedly. | 1
小心翼翼 | carefully, like wings | Very carefully. | The 翼翼 comes from the Book of Songs. | 他小心翼翼地把杯子放在桌子上。 | He put the cup carefully on the table. | 2
不言而喻 | clear without being said | Self-evident. | Used for facts that do not need to be explained. | 健康的重要性是不言而喻的。 | The importance of health is self-evident. | 2
理所当然 | as the natural thing | Only natural; taken for granted. | Used for things that seem obvious. | 帮助父母是理所当然的。 | It is only natural to help your parents. | 2
恍然大悟 | suddenly seeing the light | To suddenly understand. | Used for the moment you finally get it. | 听了老师的解释，我恍然大悟。 | After the teacher's explanation, I suddenly understood. | 2
莫名其妙 | cannot say how it is wonderful | Baffling; for no apparent reason. | Used for confusing events. | 他莫名其妙地生气了。 | He got angry for no reason. | 2
